solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gold-lined cocoons all around winged creature

indicators.note: all around tells us to turn the whole lined word round, reading it backwards
Gold-lined says the gold forms a lining, so it goes inside the other word

parts.note: to cocoon something is to wrap it up, so cocoons gives wraps
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A description of something wrapped in gold, like a jewelled pupa, around which a flying creature hovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The gold goes in first, and only then is the whole lined word turned round, so the gold reverses too.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small bird, and birds are the commonest flying creatures, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Short gust pounding earth and grass

indicators.note: A gust pounding something wraps itself round it, so the gust's letters go around the earth.

parts.note: A gust is a SQUALL; cut short to SQUAL, whose SQU goes before the E.
E is the standard abbreviation for earth.

explanation.surface: Wind shortly battering the ground and the grass on it.
explanation.walkthrough: "Grass" is the verb, not the lawn: to grass on someone is British slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeal and to grass are both slang for informing on someone, so the two verbs are straight synonyms.

clue.text: Dodge for one scrambling up mature oak

indicators.note: Scrambling things up mixes them into a new order.

parts.note: The nine letters to be rearranged.

explanation.surface: Someone dodging a task by climbing up an old oak tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodge is not a verb but the American car brand, which is why it carries a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodge is an American car manufacturer, and AUTOMAKER is the US word for one, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Rap artist beginning to tour after so long

indicators.note: after says the tour letter comes behind the goodbye, at the end

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
ta-ta is a casual British goodbye, like so long

indicators.note: beginning to tour asks for just the opening letter of that word

parts.note: first letter of tour

explanation.surface: A rapper who launches a concert tour after a long absence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rap' looks like the music, but here it means a knock. TA-TA is British slang for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-a-tat is the sound of repeated knocking on a door, and a rap is a sharp knock.

clue.text: Rose hedging runs thick, cut and bent for grafting

indicators.note: A hedge encloses a field, so hedging something puts it inside.

parts.note: Rose as in got up, WOKE; WO opens it before the R.
The rest of WOKE, closing round the R.
R is runs in cricket scoring.
THICK with its last letter cut off.

explanation.surface: A gardener grafting a rose, hedging thick growth and bending stems.
explanation.walkthrough: Every gardening word misleads: "Rose" is the past tense of rise, "bent" is an aptitude, and "grafting" is British slang for hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is an inclination and grafting is British slang for hard work, so a bent for grafting is a work ethic.

clue.text: Shot putting hole in green shed's boarding

indicators.note: Something that is boarding gets on inside a vehicle, so shed goes inside the hole.

parts.note: The hole on a putting green is the CUP; C opens it.
To shed something is to lose it.

explanation.surface: A golf shot with the ball ending by a garden shed's wooden boarding.
explanation.walkthrough: "Shot" looks like the golf stroke, but it is a camera shot; "shed" is the verb, not the garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a photograph or film shot taken from very near its subject.

clue.text: Trainee hoping to join company acted in play

indicators.note: Letters in play are loose and free to move about into a new order.

parts.note: The five letters to be rearranged.

explanation.surface: An apprentice actor who performed in a play hoping to get into a theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre company in the surface is really a military one: "acted in play" is the whole wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee in the armed forces or police, hoping to be commissioned into a company of soldiers.

clue.text: Half-cocked short-sightedness left cracks in old sporting arena

indicators.note: cracks means breaks into, so the letter for left goes inside the other word
half-cocked means skewed or out of true, so the letters of short-sightedness are knocked out of order (in fact its first half is turned round)

parts.note: myopia is the medical name for short sight

explanation.surface: A rash, short-sighted left-winger causes damage at an ancient games venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cocked' reverses only the first half, so MYO becomes OYM, giving OYMPIA; then L goes into it after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia in Greece was the site of the ancient Olympic Games, a historic venue for athletic contests.

clue.text: Spare plaster on head after last couple twisted

indicators.note: after last couple twisted means that before anything else only the final two letters swap places
on head means stood upside down, which in a down clue turns the whole word to read backwards

parts.note: Artex is a brand of textured plaster used on British ceilings

explanation.surface: A spare bandage or plaster stuck on someone's head once the last two people have been in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing ARTEX on its head gives XETRA; its original last couple, now XE at the front, are twisted back round. Artex is a British textured ceiling finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extra is additional to what is needed, which is exactly what a spare one is.

clue.text: Minute parts Turkish official stole from Tibetan native

indicators.note: Something that parts a thing splits it in two and sits in the gap.

parts.note: A PASHA is a senior Turkish official; PASH opens it.
MIN is the standard abbreviation for minute.

explanation.surface: A petty theft: a Turkish official stole something from a Tibetan.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stole" is not the past tense of steal but a shawl, and the Tibetan native is a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pashmina is a shawl woven from the fine wool of goats native to Tibet and the Himalayas, so it is a stole from a Tibetan native.

clue.text: Model turned out without any instruction

indicators.note: To model something is to shape it, so the letters are shaped into a new order.

parts.note: The nine letters to be rearranged.

explanation.surface: A model who turned up untrained.
explanation.walkthrough: "Model" is the verb, not the fashion model, so it is the anagram instruction for the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Untutored means never taught, which is being without any instruction.

clue.text: Mountain creatures retreating opposite young bears

indicators.note: Retreating is going backwards, so the letters are read right to left.
Words that bear something carry it inside them.

parts.note: Inside oppoSITE Young, read backwards.

explanation.surface: Creatures backing away from young bears across the way.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bears" looks like the animals but is the verb meaning carries, telling you the answer is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Yetis are the legendary apelike creatures said to live in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Allow retraction of confession by attorney before start of trial

indicators.note: Retracting something draws it back, so the letters are read backwards.
The start of a word is its first letter.

parts.note: An attorney confessing says I'M DA (District Attorney); reversed that is ADMI.

indicators.note: One piece placed before another comes first.

parts.note: The first letter of trial.

explanation.surface: A lawyer's confession being withdrawn before the trial begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession is the attorney announcing himself: I'M plus DA, the American District Attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to allow them in, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A lot regularly escapes working medium

definitions.text: A lot regularly escapes working medium

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged
regularly asks for every other letter, here the first, third, fifth and seventh of escapes

parts.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A great deal pours out of a psychic who is busy holding a séance.
explanation.walkthrough: ECPS (alternate letters of escapes) joins A LOT and is rearranged into ECTOPLAS, then M is added. The whole clue also describes the answer: it is what supposedly emerges from a medium at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the substance spiritualists claimed oozed from a medium in a trance during a séance.

clue.text: One's overwhelmed by pine fencing challenge in family allotment

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the one is swamped and pushed out, so other letters take its place

parts.note: kin are one's family
I is the Roman numeral for one
to pine or itch for something is to long for it
en garde is the fencer's call to get ready

explanation.surface: A family dispute over a pine fence at their garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is'. 'Pine' looks like the tree beside 'fencing', but it means long for, and en garde is the call a fencer gives before a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a rented plot for growing vegetables, much like a kitchen garden kept for the household's produce.

clue.text: Dash about house screening a day carer

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to dash is to run

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind, so the house goes around the letter a

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: Someone rushing round a house that is hiding a daytime carer from view.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British word for a semi-detached house, one of a pair sharing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after children, so she is someone who cares for others.

clue.text: Untold number in custody becoming caught by investigative action

indicators.note: One thing becoming another turns into it, so one letter changes into a different one.

parts.note: Custody is detention.
N stands for an unspecified number in maths, the first N of DETENTION.
C is caught in cricket scoring, and it takes the N's place.

explanation.surface: A suspect in custody, caught out by a police investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a crime report, but "caught" is just the letter from a cricket scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Detecting means uncovering facts by investigation, so detection names the investigative work police and sleuths carry out.

clue.text: Ribald cast includes live improv performer

indicators.note: includes means one word holds the other inside it
cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A bawdy troupe of actors features an unscripted comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the company of actors, but it is the signal to rearrange the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ad-libs speaks without a script, making things up on the spot as an improvising entertainer does.

clue.text: Rogue let out by detective on court moving charge

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector.
RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading.
CT is the standard abbreviation for court.
A cur is a scoundrel.
A room that is let out is rented.

explanation.surface: A villain released by a detective as a charge is dropped in court.
explanation.walkthrough: "Charge" belongs to the courtroom in the surface, but it is electric charge, and "on" gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct current is electric charge flowing in one direction, so it is a steady flow of moving charge.

clue.text: Bunch served up gossip in Conference Centre

indicators.note: in says the reversed gossip sits inside the core of the pear

parts.note: Conference is a variety of pear, so its centre is a core

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means read from the bottom up, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: to gas is to chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: A group of delegates dish out tittle-tattle at a meeting venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conference Centre' looks like a meeting venue, but Conference is a British pear variety, and the centre of a pear is its core.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsage is a small bunch of flowers worn on a dress or pinned at the wrist.

clue.text: Wrap up day before bagging November crop

indicators.note: Bagging something puts it in a bag, so it goes inside.

parts.note: The day before is the EVE; E opens it.
The rest of EVE.
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
To crop is to lop, to cut short.

explanation.surface: Harvesting a crop and packing it the day before November.
explanation.walkthrough: "Crop" reads as the harvest, but it is the verb meaning cut, and "November" is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to surround something on every side, which is the same act as wrapping it up.

clue.text: Whiff of flesh adjacent to butcher's outbuilding

indicators.note: Something adjacent to another sits right beside it, here the whiff after the look.

parts.note: A butcher's is a look in Cockney rhyming slang (butcher's hook, look), and a look is a GAZE.
BO is body odour, a whiff from the flesh.

explanation.surface: A smell of meat drifting from next to the butcher's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: "Butcher's" looks like the shop, but it is rhyming slang: a butcher's hook is a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden building separate from the house, so it counts as an outbuilding.

clue.text: Short period of time wasted by blocking conclusion

indicators.note: A short word falls short of its full length, losing its last letter.
Something wasted by another is lost from it, so the time goes.

parts.note: Blocking an opponent is interference.
A period of time is a TERM; cut short to TER, which is removed.

explanation.surface: A brief stretch of time lost because someone kept obstructing things.
explanation.walkthrough: "Blocking" is the noun hiding the whole answer, and a school or legal TERM is the period that goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: An inference is a conclusion reached by reasoning from evidence.

clue.text: 2 nurses jab sailor's left arm

indicators.note: nurses means holds closely, so the carmaker wraps round the other letters

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer at 2 down, an automaker, and Ford is one

indicators.note: left here means has left, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written before the sailor is removed
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A medical scene: two nurses give an injection into a seaman's left arm.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AB from JAB leaves J, which FORD holds. 'Sailor's left' reads as the sailor has left, not his left arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fjord is a long narrow inlet of the sea, and an arm of the sea is a common term for such an inlet.

clue.text: Celebrated faceless lot buried in Flanders?

indicators.note: Something buried in another is put deep inside it.

parts.note: Ned Flanders is the neighbour in The Simpsons, so Flanders suggests NED; N opens it.
LOT without its first letter.

explanation.surface: The unnamed dead of the First World War, buried in Flanders and honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: The war graves of Flanders are the obvious picture; the question mark says the Flanders is a person, Ned from The Simpsons.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known, so a noted figure is a celebrated one.

clue.text: Fizzy drink opened by you when cycling around empty spaces

indicators.note: opened by says another letter splits the word open and sits inside
cycling around means letters go round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: Someone sharing a can of pop while out on a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are cycled first, moving the opening pair to the end, and only then does the letter for you open the word up.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacua is the Latin plural of vacuum, a region containing nothing at all.

clue.text: Pair of binoculars exposed whole varieties of wildlife

indicators.note: A pair is two, so only the first two letters are taken.
Something exposed has its covering stripped, so the outer letters come off.

parts.note: The opening two letters of binoculars.
Whole is TOTAL; stripped of its outer letters it is OTA.

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher with binoculars seeing every kind of wild creature.
explanation.walkthrough: "Pair of binoculars" seems a single object, but it is two letters, and "whole" is an adjective giving TOTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The biota of a region is all its living things, its plants and animals together.

clue.text: American in hat tailed president's off-road vehicle

indicators.note: The American goes in the hat.
'tailed' cuts a letter off

parts.note: TRILBY is what 'hat' stands for
A is the standard abbreviation for American.
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower.

explanation.surface: An American president in a hat being tailed while driving a jeep.
explanation.walkthrough: "Tailed" looks like being followed, but it means docked of a tail, like a trimmed hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail bike is a light motorcycle built for riding on rough tracks, so it is an off-road vehicle.

clue.text: Maybe Prince Harry's in the act and has exited holding area

indicators.note: holding means one part wraps round another
has exited says the word and leaves the longer phrase

parts.note: caught red-handed means caught in the act
taken as written: the word and is removed

explanation.surface: A tabloid line: the royal is caught in the act and has fled the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AND from REDHANDED leaves REDHED, which then holds A. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Harry has famously ginger hair, so he is an example of a person with red hair.

clue.text: Skim head off Irish beer in festive gathering

indicators.note: The pieces go in the gathering.

parts.note: A festive gathering is a DO, a party; D opens it.

indicators.note: The head taken off a word is its first letter.

parts.note: The first letter of Irish.
A pint is a glass of beer.

explanation.surface: Skimming the froth off a pint of Guinness at a Christmas party.
explanation.walkthrough: "Skim head off" reads as one action on a beer, but the definition is just "Skim", reading a book lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip into a book is to read bits of it casually, which is to skim it.
